TRANSLATORS AS CLOSE READERS, and THE AUDIOBOOK EAR — two angles never run. Translators: Kay's French translators Élisabeth Vonarburg (Fionavar, Tigane) and, for the later novels, Mikael Cabon (verify both names) — translator interviews at Elbakin.net and ActuSF, in French, on rendering Kay's sentence, tense, register and rhythm; the justaword.fr interview (Medium-hosted; BLOCKED in the first sweep) via scribe.rip with the same path; any other translator of Kay (German, Spanish, Polish, Russian) who has spoken about the sentence. The ear: the audiobook narrator (Simon Vance narrates most of the catalogue — verify) — narrator interviews, podcasts and production notes on Kay's rhythm, cadence and dialogue, the only third-party evidence available for the cadence claims (features 23 and 27). The claims worth most say what a translator or a narrator had to DO with a Kay sentence (length, clause order, the withheld subject, the plain noun, the pause) and why.
